content.text:
This confirms it. In commit `ccf0a97dc`, the `validatePathUniqueness` flag check was moved out of the shared `validatePath()` method (which previously guarded the uniqueness check internally) and into `onCreation()` only (via the new `validateAndRenameFileOnce()` wrapper). `onModification()` was left calling `validatePath()` directly with no flag guard, so after this commit, path-uniqueness was always enforced on modification regardless of the `validatePathUniqueness` config setting — exactly the bug that `cdaa42c57` fixes by re-adding the `if (validatePathUniqueness)` guard to `onModification()`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: ccf0a97dc904c20f2fbf2df3a401e610fb0f761a

## Reasoning
(1) I traced the history of `AbstractFile.java` using `git log -S` on relevant tokens (`validatePathUniqueness`, `validatePath(securityContext, errorBuffer)`) to find when the `onModification`/`validatePath` relationship changed, then reviewed every commit touching the file between the introduction of `validatePathUniqueness` (`daac41f33`, Jan 2016) and the fix (`cdaa42c57`, Feb 2017).

(2) Originally (`daac41f33`), `validatePath()` itself contained `if (validatePathUniqueness) { ... } return true;` — so both `onCreation` and `onModification` were safe even though they called `validatePath()` unconditionally, because the guard lived inside the shared method. In `ccf0a97dc` (Feb 20, 2017), the uniqueness-check logic was refactored: the `if (validatePathUniqueness)` guard was stripped out of `validatePath()` (which now always performs the uniqueness query), and a new guard was added only around the `onCreation` path via a new `validateAndRenameFileOnce()` method. `onModification()` was left unchanged, still calling the now-unguarded `validatePath()` directly — so modification started enforcing uniqueness unconditionally, ignoring the `validatePathUniqueness` config flag.

(3) The fix commit `cdaa42c57` does exactly the complementary change: it adds `if (validatePathUniqueness) { valid = validatePath(...); }` back into `onModification`, restoring the guard that was lost in `ccf0a97dc`. The diffs of `ccf0a97dc` and `cdaa42c57` are mirror images of each other for `onModification`, which is strong direct evidence that `ccf0a97dc` is the bug-introducing commit.

I'm fairly confident in this attribution given the clear mirrored diff; the main residual uncertainty is whether there's additional unseen context (e.g., config default changes) that could implicate another commit, but nothing in the history suggests that.
